correctness.rationale: Scale weights to lambda2=1 and dualize via the geometric maximum-variance unfolding with unit distance constraints. A feasible symmetric m-page simplex embedding has hub distance s<=1 and centered variance V(s)=m+1+s^2-[((m+2)s/2)-1]^2/(m+3). Maximizing this concave quadratic yields s=1 for m=2,3,4 and s=2(m+2)/(m^2-8)<1 for m>=5, giving D_m. Explicit primal conductances x,a,b,c are nonnegative, have total D_m and yield an m-1 dimensional page-standard eigenvalue 1 and one additional axial eigenvalue 1. The quotient characteristic polynomial factors t(t-1) times a quadratic with its remaining eigenvalues strictly larger than 1, by positive shifted product and their sum >2. This matches the dual bound and proves the full optimal gap. For m>=5 the dual hub-spine edge is strictly slack (distance s<1), and complementary slackness forces x=0 in every optimizer, not merely the symmetric candidate. Independent SymPy exact quotient/weight identities and full Laplacian eigenvalues for m=2,3,4,5,6,10,20 corroborate the proof.
residual_risks: The proof assumes an undirected symmetric graph, nonnegative conductances and one uniform linear total budget; the exact spectrum certificate is not a finite-size extrapolation.
All-optima assertion concerns the common spine edge only; other optimum allocations need not be unique.

final_claim: For a graph consisting of m>=2 triangles sharing two hubs and with one pendant leaf at a hub, maximize the Laplacian algebraic connectivity over nonnegative edge weights summing to B>0. The optimum is B/D_m with D_m=m+2-m^2/[4(m+3)] for 2<=m<=4 and D_m=m+1+4/(m^2-8) for m>=5. For all m>=5 every optimizer deletes the hub-spine edge; at 2<=m<=4 a positive-spine optimizer exists.
